title: Escaping Parameter Space: Tight Generalization Bounds via Representation Quality
claim: A simple nearest-neighbor probe on learned representations, plus agreement and stability checks, yields certificates that tighten toward true error with more data.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; schematic on left, plot on right
description: Panel a) is a schematic of the method. An input X feeds a small grayscale neural network drawn as circles. An arrow branches from the network into two paths. The upper path shows the last-hidden-layer representation h(L)(x) as a tilted scatter of red, green and blue points. A kNN classifier then outputs blobs of the same colors, giving the prediction ŷ_kNN, which is labeled Q1. The lower path goes through the network output f(x) to ŷ_NN. Teal boxes mark Q2, which compares ŷ_kNN with ŷ_NN, and Q3, which is next to a circular-arrow icon for training stability. Panel b) is a line chart titled 'ResNet18 on CIFAR-10'. A red bound curve and a blue test-error curve both fall as train set size grows from 1000 to 50000. Yellow shading fills the gap between them, and double-headed arrows label the gap in percentage points, from 52.0 pp down to 8.0 pp. Grey bars at the bottom show Q1, Q2 and Q3, with Q1 the largest.
caption: Any learned feature map φ: X →Z raises three questions: Q1 Can a simple classifier in Z predict labels? Q2 Does it agree with the network? Q3 Is training stable under fold removal? a) A k-NN classifier on the last-hidden-layer representation h(L)(x) yields ˆykNN (Q1), compared against ˆyNN (Q2); a fold-trained model tests stability (Q3). b) ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10: the bound converges to within 8.0 pp of test error at n=50,000, the tightest known certificate from a deterministic network without modified training. Stacked bars show Q1 dominates: representation quality is the binding constraint.
abstract: We derive a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural We derive a tight generalization bound for deterministic neural networks based on their last hidden layer representations. By evaluating representation quality with a parameter-free $k$-nearest-neighbor ($k$-NN) classifier, our certificate avoids traditional parameter-space complexity measures, KL divergences to a posterior, weight norms, and compression. The bound is tight: trained from scratch, it reaches an 8.0 percentage point gap to test error on CIFAR-10 (ResNet-18) and yields the first non-vacuous certificates we are aware of on CIFAR-100; with frozen DINOv2 representations, it certifies at 1.4\% on CIFAR-10 and 23.1\% on 1,000-class ImageNet. It decomposes additively into three empirical, independently measurable quantities: local class geometry ($k$-NN decoder error), decoder-network agreement, and training stability. This allows the bound to act as a diagnostic tool: we demonstrate that actively destroying local class geometry eliminates generalization while leaving dataset memorization intact, identifying class geometry as a causally relevant mechanism for generalization. Finally, we show that learned representations are significantly less sensitive to weight noise than linear readouts, suggesting why parameter-space certificates often struggle to remain tight.
